source.section: Instructions PDF pp.9-10, Schedule M line 1t, questions 1 and 2 and table lines 1-4; Worksheet Step 1 lines 1-7, Step 2 lines 8-13 and instructions PDF p.9, Schedule M line 1s; Guide PDF p.12, full retirement age table; Instructions PDF p.4, RI-1040 lines 1-5; PDF p.5, lines 6-8; PDF p.13, Tax Computation Worksheet ('Use for all filing status types')

worked: Federal AGI = private pension (person 0) 30,000.00 + taxable Social Security 34,000.00 + interest 20,000.00 = 84,000.00. Federal taxable income = 84,000.00 - 15,750.00 standard deduction - 1 x 2,000.00 age 65+ = 66,250.00 (given, not tested; federal senior deduction ignored). RI-1040 line 1 federal AGI 84,000.00. Line 1s, Social Security worksheet: person 0 born 1959-03-02 (age 66). Line 3 federal AGI 84,000.00; line 4 Single; line 5 born on or before 03/01/1959: no; line 6 107,000.00; line 7 84,000.00 less than 107,000.00: yes. STOP: not eligible; modification 0.00. Line 1t: question 1 born on or before March 1, 1959: person 0 born 1959-03-02 (age 66): no; question 2 federal AGI 84,000.00 less than or equal to 107,000.00: yes. Not both yes: no table, modification 0.00. Later-births branch: born on or after 1959-03-02 and age 67 at year end; nobody can meet both in 2025, so 0.00. Line 1y total decreasing modifications = 0.00. Line 2a other-state obligations 0.00; line 2m total increasing modifications = 0.00. Schedule M page 2 line 3 net = 0.00 - 0.00 = 0.00; RI-1040 line 2 = 0.00. Line 3 modified federal AGI = 84,000.00 + (0.00) = 84,000.00. Standard Deduction and Exemption Worksheets: line 3 84,000.00 is not more than 254,250.00: the worksheets stop at line 3, full amounts. Line 4 standard deduction: 10,900.00 (Single). Line 5 = 84,000.00 - 10,900.00 = 73,100.00. Line 6 exemptions: 1 x 5,100.00 = 5,100.00. Line 7 taxable income = 73,100.00 - 5,100.00 = 68,000.00. Line 8 tax on 68,000.00 by the schedule as numbers: 68,000.00 x 0.0375 = 2550.000000 = 2,550.00. Credits 0.00 (Schedule I, Schedule II, RI earned income credit and RI-1040H are not modelled and not claimed here). Rhode Island income tax = 2,550.00. Note: Born one day after the printed date, under both the cap and the limit: not born on or before March 1, 1959, and the later-births branch needs age 67 at year end; this person is 66. Neither branch applies.
accepted_approximations: The forms state the age test for 2025 as born on or before March 1, 1959; the law is full retirement age, so that date moves each year. So that later years are not cut off, each relief has a second branch for anyone born after that date: age 67 at year end. Nobody born after the date qualifies in 2025, so 2025 is exact. People born March 2 to December 31, 1959 have a full retirement age of 66 and ten months and reach 67 in the same tax year, 2026; everyone born in 1960 or later has 67 (born January 1, 1960 uses the 1959 row and reaches both ages in 2026).
